page: Amazon Web Services c8i.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by a cache hierarchy of 48 KB L1D, 2 MB L2, and 480 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance in single-core and multi-core operations. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 2207.0 and a multi-core score of 18364.0, both placing in the strong category. Image processing and text processing benchmarks registered in the top tier, with scores of 17698.0 and 2926.0 respectively. In compression tasks, single-threaded gzip compression reached 34.25 GB/sec, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 227.98 GB/sec. For machine learning workloads, the CPU's Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) support prompt processing for a 135M LLM model at 2394.76 tokens/sec and text generation at 357.67 tokens/sec.

The c8i.8xlarge offers a high-density compute profile with DDR5 memory, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for CPU-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. However, the lack of local storage means all storage operations must rely on network-attached volumes, which may impact I/O-heavy applications. The 2.0 GB of memory per vCPU represents a lower memory-to-compute ratio, which is a tradeoff for memory-intensive database tasks, though it maintains average performance in database operations with a Passmark database score of 17347.8 and 59.81 million Redis SET operations per second.

This instance configuration is suited for compute-intensive workloads such as software compilation, image processing, text processing, static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference. It is also applicable for batch processing and network-dependent application servers that benefit from dedicated Intel Xeon compute resources.
